questions.question: 5 persons A, B, C, D and E are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). A is sitting fourth to the right of C. B is sitting second to the right of C. D is sitting to the immediate left of B. How many persons are sitting to the left of E?
questions.solution:
Logic followed here is the linear arrangement of people in a row facing **North** based on the given directions.

**Step-by-step explanation:**

1) **A is sitting fourth to the right of C:** In a row of 5 persons, this is only possible if **C** is at the 1st position (left end) and **A** is at the 5th position (right end).

2) **B is sitting second to the right of C:** This means **B** occupies the 3rd position from the left (1 + 2 = 3).

3) **D is sitting to the immediate left of B:** Since **B** is at the 3rd position, the position to its immediate left is the 2nd position, which is occupied by **D**.

4) **E is the remaining person:** The only available spot left is the 4th position, which must be occupied by **E**.

**Final Seating Arrangement:**

From the final arrangement, we can see that the persons sitting to the left of **E** (at the 4th position) are **C**, **D**, and **B**.

Total number of persons to the left of **E** = 3

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in AM) between 6 AM and 7 AM will the angle between the hour and the minute hand of a clock be 30 degrees?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The angle between the **hour hand** and the **minute hand** of a clock at any given time can be calculated using the formula:

**Angle (θ) = |30H − (11/2)M|**

Where:

**H** = the value of the hour (between 1 and 12).

**M** = the value of the minutes (between 0 and 59).

__Calculation:__

Given the time is between **6 AM** and **7 AM**, we take **H = 6**.

The required angle between the hands is **30°**.

Substitute these values into the formula:

30 = |30 × 6 − (11/2)M|

30 = |180 − 5.5M|

This equation gives two possible cases:

**Case 1: When the minute hand is behind the hour hand**

180 − 5.5M = 30

5.5M = 180 − 30

5.5M = 150

M = 150/5.5 ≈ **27.27 minutes**

This corresponds to approximately **6:27 AM**.

**Case 2: When the minute hand has crossed the hour hand**

5.5M − 180 = 30

5.5M = 180 + 30

5.5M = 210

M = 210/5.5 = 420/11 ≈ **38.18 minutes**

This corresponds to approximately **6:38 AM**.

Comparing the results with the given options, the time **6:38 AM** is listed as an option.

Hence, the correct answer is **6:38**.

questions.question: A clock shows the correct time at 8 AM. The clock gains 2 seconds every 6 minutes. What time (in PM) will it show at 8 PM the same day?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The time interval from **8 AM** to **8 PM** on the same day is **12 hours**.

Total time in minutes = 12 × 60 = **720 minutes**.

__Calculation:__

Given that the **clock** gains **2 seconds** in every **6 minutes**.

Rate of gain = 2 ÷ 6 = 1/3 **seconds per minute**.

Total gain in 720 minutes = 720 × 1/3 = **240 seconds**.

Converting the total gain into minutes: 240 ÷ 60 = **4 minutes**.

Now, the actual time is **8 PM**.

Time shown by the clock = Actual time + Total gain

Time shown = 8:00:00 + 4 minutes = **8:04:00**.

Hence, the correct answer is **8:04:00**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Clock gain in **1 hour** (60 minutes):

6 minutes = 2 seconds

60 minutes = (2 ÷ 6) × 60 = **20 seconds**.

Total gain in **12 hours** = 12 × 20 = **240 seconds**.

Total gain in minutes = 240 ÷ 60 = **4 minutes**.

Therefore, the time the clock will show at **8 PM** is **8:04:00**.

questions.question: Which constitutional amendment gave constitutional status to cooperative societies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**97th Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **97th Constitutional Amendment Act** of **2011** was enacted to provide constitutional status and protection to **cooperative societies** in India, coming into effect on **February 15, 2012**.
 
• It introduced **Article 19(1)(c)** in the **Fundamental Rights** section (Part III), which explicitly grants citizens the right to form **cooperative societies**.
 
• The amendment inserted **Article 43B** into the **Directive Principles of State Policy** (Part IV), directing the State to promote the voluntary formation, autonomous functioning, democratic control, and professional management of cooperative societies.
 
• It added a new **Part IXB** to the Constitution, titled **The Co-operative Societies**, spanning **Articles 243ZH to 243ZT**, which regulates the incorporation, number and term of members of the board, and the auditing of accounts.
 
• The primary objective was to ensure that cooperatives across the country operate in a professional and democratic manner, reducing **political interference** and improving economic efficiency for farmers and small-scale producers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **73rd Amendment Act, 1992**:

 
 
• Granted constitutional status to **Panchayati Raj Institutions** by adding **Part IX** and the **Eleventh Schedule** to the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act, 2002**:
 
 
• Inserted **Article 21A**, making the **Right to Education** a fundamental right for children between the ages of **6 and 14 years**.
 
 
 
• **91st Amendment Act, 2003**:
 
 
• Limited the size of the **Council of Ministers** to **15 percent** of the total strength of the **Lok Sabha** or **State Legislative Assembly** and strengthened **Anti-Defection** laws.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Cooperation**:
 
 
• In **July 2021**, the Union Government created this ministry to provide a separate administrative, legal, and policy framework for strengthening the cooperative movement under the vision of **Sahkar se Samriddhi**.

questions.question: Which musical instrument is commonly used during Giddha performances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Giddha** is a popular folk dance of women in the **Punjab** region of India and Pakistan, traditionally performed during social gatherings and festivals like **Teeyan** and **Baisakhi**.
 
• The **Dhol**, a large double-sided barrel drum, is the primary musical instrument that provides the rhythmic foundation for the dance. While **Bhangra** (the male counterpart) uses a larger version, Giddha performances often feature the **Dhol** or its smaller variant, the **Dholki**.
 
• The instrument is typically constructed from a wooden barrel (often **Mango** or **Sheesham** wood) with animal hide stretched over both ends, played using wooden sticks or hands to produce deep bass and sharp treble sounds.
 
• The rhythm of the **Dhol** complements the **Boliyan** (folk singing), where the beat accelerates during the **clapping** sequences, which is a signature element of the Giddha performance.
 
• In a traditional setup, the woman playing the **Dhol** sits in the center of a circle formed by other dancers, who move in rhythmic patterns mimicking daily village chores like churning milk or spinning yarn.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tabla**

 
 
• A set of two small drums used predominantly in **Hindustani classical music** and **Sufi** devotional songs.
 
• It consists of the **Dayan** (treble) and **Bayan** (bass) and is known for its complex finger-tapping techniques rather than the loud, rustic beats required for folk dances.
 
 
 
• **Harmonium**
 
 
• A keyboard-based reed instrument that produces sound by blowing air through bellows; it is a staple in **Ghazals**, **Qawwalis**, and **Kirtans**.
 
• While it provides melodic support in various Punjabi folk genres, it is not the lead rhythmic instrument for Giddha.
 
 
 
• **Sarangi**
 
 
• A short-necked, bowed string instrument made of wood with a skin-covered soundbox, often used to accompany vocalists in **classical** and **folk ballads**.
 
• It is revered for its ability to mimic the nuances of the human voice but is rarely used in the high-energy percussion-centric environment of Giddha.

questions.question: Which physiographic division is famous for its rich alluvial soil and high population density?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Northern Plains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Northern Plains** of India are formed by the massive depositional work of three major river systems: the **Indus**, the **Ganga**, and the **Brahmaputra**, along with their numerous tributaries.
 
• This physiographic division covers an area of approximately **7 lakh square kilometers**, extending about **2,400 kilometers** in length and **240 to 320 kilometers** in width.
 
• The region is characterized by a deep cover of **alluvial soil**, which has been deposited over millions of years in a vast basin situated at the foothills of the **Himalayas**.
 
• The **alluvium** is extremely fertile and rich in minerals, which, combined with a perennial **water supply** and a **favorable climate**, makes this area the most agriculturally productive part of the country, often referred to as the **granary of India**.
 
• Due to its high **agricultural output** and the flat nature of the terrain, which facilitates easy **transportation** and **urbanization**, the Northern Plains have the **highest population density** among all physiographic divisions in India.
 
• The plains are further categorized into the **Bhabar**, **Terai**, **Bhangar**, and **Khadar** regions based on the variations in relief and the nature of the soil deposits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peninsular Plateau**:

 
 
• It is a **tableland** composed of old crystalline, **igneous**, and **metamorphic rocks**, formed due to the breaking and drifting of the **Gondwana land**.
 
• This region is known for its **black soil** (Regur) in the **Deccan Trap**, which is ideal for cotton cultivation but is not as densely populated as the Northern Plains.
 
 
 
• **Coastal Plains**:
 
 
• These are narrow coastal strips running along the **Arabian Sea** on the west and the **Bay of Bengal** on the east.
 
• The **Eastern Coastal Plain** features large deltas formed by rivers like the **Mahanadi**, **Godavari**, **Krishna**, and **Kaveri**, which are fertile but much smaller in scale compared to the Northern Plains.
 
 
 
• **Himalayas**:
 
 
• These are **geologically young** and **structurally fold mountains** that stretch across the northern borders of India.
 
• The rugged terrain, steep slopes, and harsh climatic conditions make it unsuitable for intensive agriculture, resulting in a **sparse population density**.

questions.question: Who discovered the electron in 1897 through cathode ray experiments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**J.J. Thomson**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sir Joseph John Thomson**, a British physicist, is credited with the discovery of the **electron** in **1897** through his series of experiments with **cathode ray tubes**.
 
• He observed that **cathode rays** were deflected by both **electric** and **magnetic fields**, suggesting they were composed of **negatively charged particles** rather than waves.
 
• By measuring the degree of deflection, Thomson calculated the **charge-to-mass ratio (e/m)** of these particles and found it to be constant, regardless of the material of the electrodes or the gas in the tube.
 
• He concluded that these particles, which he initially termed **corpuscles**, were a fundamental part of all atoms, thereby proving that the **atom** was divisible.
 
• Following this discovery, he proposed the **Plum Pudding Model** of the atom in **1904**, where negative electrons were embedded in a uniform sphere of positive charge.
 
• Thomson was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics** in **1906** for his work on the conduction of electricity by gases and the discovery of the electron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ernest Rutherford**:

 
 
• He is known as the **father of nuclear physics**.
 
• Conducted the famous **Gold Foil Experiment** in **1911**, which led to the discovery of the **atomic nucleus**.
 
• He also discovered the **proton** and established that most of the atom's mass is concentrated in the center.
 
 
 
• **Niels Bohr**:
 
 
• Developed the **Bohr Model** of the atom in **1913**.
 
• He proposed that **electrons** revolve around the nucleus in specific **quantized energy levels** or shells.
 
 
 
• **James Chadwick**:
 
 
• He discovered the **neutron** in **1932**.
 
• The neutron is a **subatomic particle** with no net electric charge, located within the **atomic nucleus** along with protons.

• **Starred Questions** are those for which a member desires an **oral answer** on the floor of the House. These are distinguished by an **asterisk mark**. Because the answer is delivered orally, **supplementary questions** can be asked by members with the permission of the Speaker or Chairman. Hence, Starred Question is a valid type.
 
• **Unstarred Questions** are those for which a **written explanation** is required. These are not specifically marked with an asterisk, and the written reply is deemed to be laid on the table of the House by the concerned Minister at the end of **Question Hour**. • **Short Notice Questions** relate to matters of **urgent public importance** and can be asked with a notice shorter than the standard **ten clear days**. These questions are answered **orally**, provided the Minister concerned agrees to answer at short notice. Hence, Short Notice is a valid type.
 
• The Indian parliamentary system does not recognize a category formally named **Urgent Question**. While the **Short Notice Question** addresses urgent matters, the terminology 'Urgent Question' is not used in the **Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business** of the **Lok Sabha** or **Rajya Sabha**. Hence, Urgent Question is not a type of parliamentary question.

questions.question: A bag contains red and blue balls in the ratio 7:5. If there are 60 balls in total, how many are red?

Comparison of Proper Fractions

Same Numerator Rule

questions.question: 95P8 is divisible by 6. What is the value of P?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a number to be **divisible by 6**, it must be divisible by both **2** and **3**.

The number **95P8** ends in **8**, so it is already **divisible by 2**.

For **divisibility by 3**, the **sum of digits** (9 + 5 + P + 8 = **22 + P**) must be a multiple of **3**.

Checking options: 22 + **2** = 24, which is divisible by **3**.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The number **95P8** is divisible by **6**.

**Formula Used:** A number is **divisible by 6** if it satisfies the divisibility rules of both **2** and **3**.

⇒ **Divisibility rule of 2:** The last digit of the number must be **even** (0, 2, 4, 6, or 8).

⇒ In **95P8**, the unit digit is **8**, which is even. Thus, the number is divisible by **2** for any value of **P**.

⇒ **Divisibility rule of 3:** The **sum of all digits** of the number must be divisible by **3**.

⇒ Sum of digits = 9 + 5 + **P** + 8 = **22 + P**

⇒ For the number to be divisible by **3**, **22 + P** must be a multiple of 3 (24, 27, 30, ...).

⇒ If **22 + P = 24**, then **P = 2**.

⇒ If **22 + P = 27**, then **P = 5**.

⇒ If **22 + P = 30**, then **P = 8**.

⇒ Among the given options (0, 2, 4, 6), only **P = 2** satisfies the condition.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3.

Divisibility by 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the last two digits of the number are divisible by 4.

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.

questions.question: Average runs of a player in 15 matches is 38. How much runs he must score in the next match to make his average 40?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Increase in **average** required = 40 − 38 = 2 runs

Total matches after next game = 16

Runs required = New Average + (Old Matches × Increase)

Required runs = 40 + (15 × 2) = 40 + 30 = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70 runs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of 15 matches = 38, Target average of 16 matches = 40.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/627d7d62ff9ff0b766ae19d9d86fbe96408f87c1cb86482bdae8ec26ca75a0af.png] 

**Formula:** Total Runs = Average × Number of Matches

⇒ Total runs in 15 matches = 15 × 38

⇒ Total runs (15 matches) = 570 runs

⇒ Total runs required for 16 matches = 16 × 40

⇒ Total runs (16 matches) = 640 runs

⇒ Runs needed in 16th match = Total runs (16 matches) − Total runs (15 matches)

⇒ Runs in 16th match = 640 − 570 = 70 runs

**∴ The correct answer is 70 runs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Basic Concept

Average is the sum of all observations divided by the number of observations. **Average = Sum ÷ Count**.

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all values from the average is always zero. If the average increases, the new value must be **New Avg + (Previous Count × Increase)**.

Inclusion/Exclusion Rule

When a new member joins and the average increases, the value of the new member = **Old Average + (New Total Strength × Increase in Average)**.

questions.question: Average of 12 consecutive odd natural numbers is 36. The just previous and the just next odd natural number to these 12 odd natural numbers are also included. What will be the new average?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In any **Arithmetic Progression (AP)**, if an equal number of terms are added symmetrically to both the start and the end, the **Average** remains unchanged.

The 12 **consecutive odd numbers** form an AP with a common difference of 2.

Adding the **just previous** and **just next** odd number is a perfectly **symmetrical addition** around the central value.

Original Average = 36.

New Average = 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of 12 **consecutive odd natural numbers** is 36.

**Formula Used:** Average of numbers in **Arithmetic Progression** = (First term + Last term) ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1cad9c786e4ce1dd425162d5bbe907a228363539763e6eb80a0cc2d631f6d845.png] 

⇒ For 12 consecutive odd numbers, the average 36 lies between the 6th and 7th term.

⇒ Middle terms = 36 − 1 and 36 + 1 = 35 and 37.

⇒ First term (a) = 35 − (5 × 2) = 25.

⇒ Last term (l) = 37 + (5 × 2) = 47.

⇒ Just previous odd number = 25 − 2 = 23.

⇒ Just next odd number = 47 + 2 = 49.

⇒ New Average = (New First Term + New Last Term) ÷ 2

⇒ New Average = (23 + 49) ÷ 2 = 72 ÷ 2 = 36.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression (AP) Property

For any **AP**, the average of n terms is always (a + l) ÷ 2, where a is the first term and l is the last term.

Symmetrical Addition Rule

Adding or removing terms symmetrically from the center of an **AP** does not change the **Arithmetic Mean**.

Sum of Consecutive Odd Numbers

The sum of first n **odd numbers** starting from 1 is n². For any other sequence, sum = n × Average.

questions.question: What is the total number of positive factors of 200?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Prime Factorization** of 200 = 2³ × 5².

To find the total number of **positive factors**, add 1 to each exponent and multiply the results.

Total factors = (3 + 1) × (2 + 1) = 4 × 3 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The number is 200.

**Formula Used:** If a number N can be expressed in prime factorization as N = pa × qb × rc..., then the total number of **positive factors** is given by (a + 1)(b + 1)(c + 1)...

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e273ebc1fc48755e58675cb4cc07864f50232ee601f204bfeb23f0630298754c.png] 

⇒ Prime factorization of 200: 200 = 2 × 100

⇒ 200 = 2 × 2 × 50

⇒ 200 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 25

⇒ 200 = 2³ × 5²

⇒ Here, p = 2, a = 3 and q = 5, b = 2.

⇒ Total number of factors = (3 + 1) × (2 + 1)

⇒ Total number of factors = 4 × 3 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Factors

The sum of all factors of N = pa × qb is calculated as [(pa⁺¹ − 1) / (p − 1)] × [(qb⁺¹ − 1) / (q − 1)].

Number of Odd and Even Factors

For N = 2a × pb × qc, the number of **odd factors** is (b+1)(c+1)... and the number of **even factors** is a × (b+1)(c+1)...

Product of Factors

The product of all factors of a number N is equal to N⁽Total Factors / ²⁾.

• अतः, यह संपूर्ण विचार संस्थाओं के मध्य बेहतर समन्वय के सिद्धांत को ही दर्शाता है।
